purpose: One connected eight-moment acceptance evaluation of the preserved ORIGINAL F01 candidate. All actions, knowledge, outcomes and changes are predetermined authority fixtures, not implemented gameplay. No generated prose establishes authority.
chronology: E1: Player reaches the riverside depot receiving office to inquire about an overdue paper crate for Tern Bindery. Ordinary working afternoon, no deadline or immediate danger.
E2: Clerk Sela distinguishes her own morning receipt of the crate from porter Orin's unverified report that he moved it to the covered landing.
E3: Sela substantively answers the follow-up about identifying the crate and checking paperwork; authorizes looking at a dispatch slip in the office cabinet.

E4: During the authorized conditional slip inspection, a brittle corner tears before the player recognizes the risk. Player stops on recognition, after reading only the covered-landing destination. Inspection costs five minutes and leaves a small corner tear.
E5: Scheduled unloading blocks the direct receiving lane. Player separately authorizes and completes movement via the open east walkway to the covered landing, taking a few minutes.
E6: Inspection at the landing yields overlapping wheel marks but no usable trail or identified crate. It costs a few minutes.

E7: In the adjacent cart lane a distinct trail is actually found and followed across soft ground, then lost at paving. No link to the paper crate is established. Player ends in the paved yard after about ten minutes.

E8: Player returns to Sela and asks for the ledger's record. An accessible reliable entry supports historical handover to the covered-landing crew, not current whereabouts. Prior report remains attributed. No crate recovery or onward player decision is established.

structural: Original candidate and instruction bytes match original A-D evaluation, not revised candidate
Eight calls maximum, one per moment, no retries or post-result changes
Exact requests, outputs, metadata and immutable material preserved
Only explicit context reaches original candidate; no evaluation criteria or generated history
fidelity: Preserve authorization, perceptual chronology, accepted results, costs and document damage
Distinguish Sela's firsthand account from Orin's report and later ledger evidence
Wheel marks without a usable trail differ from a trail actually found, followed and lost
Do not infer crate identity, owner, destination or current availability from unidentified cart traces
Revisit relevant history with its original source and temporal scope; do not manufacture re-verification requirements
experience: Read all eight moments in order with the player actions; assess one experience rather than independent phrase matches
Useful substantive NPC exchange, natural uncertainty, responsive follow-up and coherent transitions
Appropriate detail and emphasis without repeated scene inventories or mechanical boundary/status endings
Consider qualitative time/distance and direct first-person NPC speech as historical presentation guidance/owner preferences, without adding them to the unchanged original prompt
No minimum length, obligatory decorative description, dramatic escalation or required exact wording
review_criteria.decision: Owner experiential review remains necessary. Neither factual correctness alone nor isolated style preferences automatically accept or reject F01. This one sequence does not establish extended-gameplay reliability or architecture adequacy.

moments.focus: Orient the delivery inquiry as the player reaches the depot receiving office.

player_intent.objective: Find out what happened to the overdue paper crate intended for Tern Bindery.
player_intent.method: Walk to the riverside depot and present the delivery note at the receiving desk.
player_intent.authorization: The player authorized this walk and inquiry only, not collecting a crate or entering restricted storage.

developments.meaning: After a short walk, you enter the receiving office and present the Tern Bindery delivery note. Clerk Sela is at the desk and has agreed to hear the inquiry. An open door leads toward the working yard; ordinary river and depot sounds carry inside. The crate has not reached the bindery, and its current location is not yet known to you.
developments.authority: World Simulation; Action & Resolution; Actors & Social Dynamics
developments.source: Stipulated accepted arrival, delivery state and clerk presence/cooperation
developments.access: Player experiences arrival and sees/hears this public office scene

knowledge_limits: The delivery note does not establish the crate's current depot location or any misconduct.
unresolved: Where the paper crate is now and why delivery is overdue.
boundaries: No deadline, immediate danger, theft, hostile actor or special urgency is established.
Do not choose the player's next question or move beyond the receiving office.

moments.focus: Deliver Sela's accepted answer to whether the bindery crate arrived and where it went.

player_intent.objective: Ask Sela whether the paper crate arrived and where it was taken.
player_intent.method: Continue the inquiry at the receiving desk.
player_intent.authorization: Only this question is authorized; no pursuit, accusation or crate collection.

developments.meaning: Sela answers that she personally checked in the bindery's paper crate this morning. Porter Orin later told her he had wheeled it to the covered landing. Sela did not witness Orin moving it and has not checked where the crate is now.
developments.source: Sela's own firsthand receipt account; separate Orin-to-Sela movement report
developments.time: Reply now about receipt and reported movement earlier today
developments.access: Player hears Sela's account; neither player nor Sela has current observation of the crate

continuity.meaning: You remain at Sela's receiving desk with the Tern Bindery delivery note; she is cooperating with the inquiry.
continuity.source: Stipulated continuing office exchange after E1

knowledge_limits: Sela can speak firsthand about receipt, not firsthand about Orin's movement or the crate's current location.
unresolved: Whether the reported move occurred and where the crate is now.

No disappearance cause, dishonesty or deliberate obstruction is established.

moments.focus: Answer the meaningful follow-up about recognizing the crate and checking its dispatch paperwork.

player_intent.objective: Ask how to identify the paper crate and whether its dispatch slip can be checked.
player_intent.method: Ask Sela at the same desk.
player_intent.authorization: The player asks for information and permission; inspection has not yet begun.

developments.meaning: Sela says the crate carries a blue crane stamp and two iron bands; she saw these when she received it. She explains that its dispatch slip is in the cabinet beside her desk and gives permission to inspect that slip. She knows the identifying marks and cabinet location firsthand. She does not supply a new claim about the crate's current location.
developments.source: Sela's accepted substantive answer and explicit inspection permission
developments.time: Current reply; identifying observation earlier today
developments.access: Player hears the answer and can see the indicated office cabinet

continuity.meaning: Sela personally received the crate; the covered-landing move is still Orin's report relayed by her. You remain at her desk with the delivery note.

knowledge_limits: Identification marks permit recognizing a matching crate; they do not locate it or authorize taking property.
unresolved: What the dispatch slip actually says; current crate whereabouts.
boundaries: Do not start inspecting before the separately authorized next action.
No promise to retrieve the crate or permission to open a crate is established.

player_intent.objective: Read the dispatch destination without damaging the slip.
player_intent.method: Carefully lift the slip from the cabinet to read it.
player_intent.authorization: The player authorized inspection with Sela's permission, stopping if the paper began to tear.
constraints: Do not knowingly continue handling the slip after recognizing a tear.

developments.meaning: You read the destination line, which says covered landing. A brittle corner then tears before you notice the paper's fragility. On recognizing the tear you stop handling it and leave the slip in the cabinet. No further text is read. The corner remains torn. The inspection has taken five minutes. You did not recognize the risk beforehand or choose to continue after noticing damage.

developments.time: Just completed; recognition follows the tear
developments.access: Direct player experience and partial document reading

continuity.meaning: You are at the cabinet beside Sela's desk. She authorized inspecting the dispatch slip; the blue crane stamp and two iron bands came from her earlier firsthand account. Orin's movement report was not itself verified by that account.

E1: Ordinary delivery objective, legitimate clerk presence, useful orientation without new urgency
E2: Firsthand receipt versus relayed movement; substantive information without current-location confirmation
E3: Useful identification and permission reply, no premature inspection or invented retrieval promise
E4: Destination line read before corner tear; fragility recognized afterward; stop on recognition; tear and elapsed effort retained
E5: Independent scheduled development changes available path; authorized movement ends at landing; no recap or fictional emergency
